zh.title: 一句話兩種語言
zh.question: 同一句結論，中英兩套文案。契約是字對字，還是判斷、否定和數字不能漂。

analyst.answer: 兩種語言要同一判斷。數字、否定、主語不能漂。
analyst.review:
「最容易被弄丟的是「不」。少一個不，結論就反了。」
對齊的是判斷，這半句成立。語感不同不能當成判斷不同，這半句也成立。兩句沒有說主語。主語換了，語感可以仍然自然，判斷已經是另一個建議。對齊判斷時，主語和否定、數字同一級，不能留在語感裡。
brief: 契約不是字對字。契約是同一判斷：數字、否定、主語不能漂。語感不同，推不出判斷不同。主語換了，就不是翻譯，是另一個建議。
兩種語言要同一判斷。同一判斷的意思是：主語相同、否定相同、數字相同、條件相同。語感可以不同。判斷不能為了語感漂。漂了，讀者會按自己的語言執行另一個結論。
最容易漂的是「不」。中文少一個不，英文多一個 not，兩邊就相反。其次是條件：中文寫「超標再換」，英文寫成「可以考慮換」，條件被刪掉了。刪條件和改否定一樣，都是另一個決策。
兩種語言的主語、否定或數字有一個不一致，這席撤回「這是同一句」。語感差異不構成這個反例。

researcher.answer: 翻譯不能加入另一語沒有的條件，也不能刪掉有的。
researcher.review:
「兩句都要能複述，而且複述出來是同一件事。」
像人話，推不出可以加一句原文沒有的讓步。讓步是條件。另一語沒有這個條件，加上去就不是翻譯。這句若被收成「不好聽就可以加讓步」，契約被語感改掉了。典故同樣：更好聽，也是另一句。
brief: 翻譯不能加入另一語沒有的條件，也不能刪掉有的。典故會讓一句更好聽，也會讓它變成另一句。加進去的讓步如果原文沒有，就是新條件。
翻譯不能加入另一語沒有的條件，也不能刪掉有的。我沒有來源把某一句成語寫成另一句更強的技術斷言。成語如果帶了新的範圍，它就不是翻譯，是新情報。
專有詞要對上，不要意譯成一個更寬的類。SQLite 不要寫成「資料庫」。門控不要寫成「智能選擇」。寬的類會讓另一種語言的讀者以為範圍變了。範圍變了，契約就破了。
任一語比另一語多一個條件、少一個條件，或靠典故增加了原句沒有的讓步，這席撤回這條翻譯。

engineer.answer: 中英必須同一組欄位。缺一句就不要用另一語補。
engineer.review:
「數字、單位、大小方向，兩種語言必須相同。」
數字、單位、方向必須相同，這句是值的契約。它不代替欄位契約。欄位缺了，另一語有值也不許補。這句若被收成「值相同就可以缺欄位」，失敗被換成了隱含繼承。缺一句就不要用另一語補。
brief: 中英必須同一組欄位。缺一句就失敗，不要用另一語補。欄位對上還不夠：數字欄位的值也必須相同。缺了可以失敗，值反了會騙。
中英必須是同一組欄位，不是兩篇各自寫完再互相補。缺一句就不要用另一語補。補了，兩種語言的契約就變成「誰最後寫誰算」。最後寫的人通常看不見自己加了條件。
實作上把判斷存成欄位，再渲染成兩種語言。欄位裡有否定、數字、條件。渲染層可以調整詞序，不可以改欄位。改欄位的翻譯，該在檢查時失敗，而不是上線後等人發現兩邊建議相反。
任一語缺欄位，或同一欄位的值不同，這席拒絕發布。不接受用另一語把洞補上。

critic.answer: 最容易被弄丟的是「不」。少一個不，結論就反了。
critic.review:
「先鎖判斷，再寫中英。不要為了語感改判斷。」
先鎖判斷再寫兩語，這句沒有把「不」列進要鎖的東西。判斷如果只鎖了肯定句，否定會在第二語裡為了順被拿掉。要鎖的包括否定。不要為了一種語感改判斷，尤其不要改「不」。
brief: 最容易被弄丟的是「不」。少一個不，結論就反了。先鎖判斷再寫兩語。不要為了一種語感改判斷。語感順而否定丟了，比缺譯更糟：缺了可以失敗，反了會騙。
最容易被弄丟的是「不」。少一個不，結論就反了。我對翻譯的檢查先數否定，再數數字，再看條件還在不在。文采排在這三項後面。
「可以考慮」「建議關注」「在適當時候」這類詞，如果另一語是一個硬條件，就是把硬條件譯軟了。譯軟是刪除。刪除不因語氣禮貌而通過。
任一語少了一個「不」或多了一個「不」，這席要求該句不能發布。不接受為了順而留著。

strategist.answer: 先鎖判斷，再寫中英。不要為了語感改判斷。
strategist.review:
「兩種語言要同一判斷。數字、否定、主語不能漂。」
數字、否定、主語不能漂，這句是契約的內容。它沒有寫順序。若先寫一種語言再讓另一種遷就語感，主語會在第二步漂掉。先鎖判斷再寫兩語。不要為了一種語感改判斷，包括不要改主語。
brief: 先鎖判斷，再寫中英。不要為了語感改判斷。主語換了，就不是翻譯，是另一個建議。鎖判斷時主語、否定、條件一起鎖，不能只鎖最好聽的肯定句。
先鎖判斷，再寫中英。不要為了語感改判斷。語感是某一種語言裡怎樣更像人話。人話如果把「不換」說成「再觀察」，策略就變了。變了的策略不是更好的翻譯，是另一個策略。
兩個語言的讀者要能執行同一個動作。動作不同，就不是雙語，是兩份建議。兩份建議會在團隊裡各找支持者，最後沒有人知道哪一份算數。
若一種語言的主語和另一種不同，這席撤回「判斷已鎖」。語感再順也不簽。

writer.answer: 兩句都要能複述，而且複述出來是同一件事。
writer.review:
「翻譯不能加入另一語沒有的條件，也不能刪掉有的。」
不能加入另一語沒有的條件，這句禁止增條件。它沒有禁止用典故把條件換成聽起來像同一件、其實是另一件的事。典故會讓一句更好聽，也會讓它變成另一句。複述出來必須仍是同一件事，不能只是同一種情緒。
brief: 兩句都要能複述，而且複述出來是同一件事。像人話不能靠加一句原文沒有的讓步，也不能靠典故把條件換成聽眾熟悉的另一個條件。
兩句都要能複述，而且複述出來是同一件事。複述測試比對照詞彙有用。請一個只讀中文的人和一個只讀英文的人各說一次他們會做什麼。兩次不一樣，翻譯就失敗，不管句子多順。
我可以換詞序、拆長句、重複主語。我不可以為了順口刪掉「不」，也不可以為了強調加上另一語沒有的「必須」。順口和強調都不是新欄位的理由。
兩種語言的複述對不上同一判斷，這席不簽。不好聽可以改寫，不能改判斷。

quant.answer: 數字、單位、大小方向，兩種語言必須相同。
quant.review:
「中英必須同一組欄位。缺一句就不要用另一語補。」
同一組欄位，推不出欄位裡的值相同。欄位都叫「上限」，一語是 8、一語是 5，欄位對上了，判斷反了或漂了。欄位對上還不夠。數字欄位的值也必須相同。方向反了比缺譯更糟。
brief: 數字、單位、大小方向，兩種語言必須相同。方向反了比缺譯更糟。缺了可以失敗，反了會騙。8 不能在另一語變成 5，大於不能變成小於。
數字、單位、大小方向，兩種語言必須相同。中文的「不超過」，英文如果寫成 more than，方向就反了。單位從毫秒寫成秒，閘門就差一千倍。這兩種漂都不屬於文采。
沒有出現的數，兩種語言都不加。不能因為英文句需要一個例子，就補一個中文沒有的百分比。例子是新測量。新測量不從翻譯裡產生。
任一語的數字、單位或比較方向和另一語不同，這席拒絕發布。不接受「大概同一個數」。

chair.answer: 一句話兩種語言，契約是同一判斷。否定、數字和條件不能在翻譯裡增刪。
brief: 契約不是字對字，是同一判斷。分析師搶紅隊的那句成立：語感不同不是判斷不同，但主語必須和否定、數字同一級，不能留在語感裡。紅隊搶策略家的那句成立：要鎖的包括「不」。少一個不，結論就反了。
策略家搶分析師的那句成立：先鎖判斷再寫兩語，否則主語在第二步漂掉。情報官搶表達者的那句成立：典故和額外讓步都會把一句變成另一句。表達者搶情報官的那句成立：禁止增條件，還要禁止用典故把條件換成另一件事。
工程師搶量化員的那句成立：值的契約不代替欄位契約，缺一句不能用另一語補。量化員搶工程師的那句成立：欄位對上不夠，值必須相同。方向反了比缺譯更糟。缺了可以失敗，反了會騙。
可執行的是：先鎖判斷，再寫中英。否定、數字、單位、方向、主語、條件都不能增刪。缺欄位就失敗，不用另一語補。語感可以不同。判斷不能漂。

en.title: One line, two languages
en.question: One verdict, two languages. Is the contract word-for-word, or that the judgment, the negation, and the numbers must not drift?

analyst.answer: Both languages carry the same judgment. Numbers, negations, and the subject must not drift.
analyst.review:
"The easiest word to lose is not. Drop it and the verdict flips."
The half that says align the judgment holds. The half that says a different ear is not a different judgment also holds. Neither half mentions the subject. Change the subject, and the line can still sound natural while the judgment has become another recommendation. When aligning the judgment, the subject sits at the same rank as the negation and the numbers. It cannot be left inside the ear.
brief: The contract is not word-for-word. The contract is the same judgment: numbers, negations, and the subject must not drift. A different ear does not entail a different judgment. Change the subject, and it is not a translation. It is another recommendation.

The two languages have to carry the same judgment. Same judgment means the same subject, the same negation, the same numbers, and the same conditions. Tone may differ. The judgment may not drift for the sake of tone. If it drifts, a reader will carry out a different verdict in their own language.

What drifts first is 'not'. Drop one 不 in Chinese, or add one not in English, and the two sides are opposites. Conditions drift next: Chinese says 'migrate when the line is crossed', English says 'consider migrating', and the condition is gone. Deleting a condition is a different decision, the same as flipping a negation.
If the subject, the negation, or a number differs between the two languages, this seat withdraws "this is the same sentence." A difference of ear is not that counterexample.

researcher.answer: A translation cannot add a condition the other language lacks, or drop one it has.
researcher.review:
"Both lines must be repeatable, and the repetition must be the same claim."
Sounding human does not entail adding a concession the original lacked. A concession is a condition. The other language does not have that condition, so adding it is not a translation. Closed as "if it sounds bad, add a concession," the contract has been retuned by ear. An allusion is the same case: nicer, and also a different line.
brief: A translation cannot add a condition the other language lacks, or drop one it has. A local allusion makes a line nicer and also makes it a different line. A concession that was not in the original is a new condition.

A translation may not add a condition the other language does not have, and it may not delete one that it does. I have no source for turning an idiom into a stronger technical claim. If the idiom brings a new scope, it is not a translation. It is new intelligence.

Name the thing, do not paraphrase it into a wider class. SQLite should not become 'a database'. The gate should not become 'intelligent selection'. A wider class teaches the reader in the other language that the scope changed. If the scope changed, the contract is broken.
If either language has one more condition, one fewer condition, or a concession added by allusion that the original lacked, this seat withdraws that translation.

engineer.answer: Chinese and English must share the same fields. Don't fill a gap from the other tongue.
engineer.review:
"The numeral, the unit, and the direction of comparison must match."
The numeral, the unit, and the direction must match. That is the contract on values. It does not replace the contract on fields. If a field is missing, a value in the other language may not fill it. Closed as "if the values match, a field may be missing," a failure has been replaced by implied inheritance. Don't fill a gap from the other tongue.
brief: Chinese and English must share the same fields. A missing line fails. Do not fill it from the other tongue. Matching fields is not enough: the value in a number field must match too. Missing can fail. A flipped value deceives.

Chinese and English have to be the same set of fields, not two essays written separately and then used to patch each other. If a sentence is missing, do not fill it from the other language. Once you do, the contract becomes 'whoever wrote last wins'. The person who wrote last usually cannot see the condition they added.

Store the judgment as fields, then render both languages. The fields hold the negation, the numbers, and the conditions. The render may change word order. It may not change a field. A translation that changes a field should fail the check, not ship and wait for someone to notice the two sides recommend opposite moves.
If either language lacks a field, or the same field has a different value, this seat refuses to publish. Filling the hole from the other tongue is not accepted.

critic.answer: The easiest word to lose is not. Drop it and the verdict flips.
critic.review:
"Lock the judgment, then write both. Don't change it to suit one language."
Lock the judgment, then write both. That line does not list "not" among the things to lock. If the judgment locks only the affirmative, the negation will be removed in the second language to make it smooth. What gets locked includes the negation. Do not retune the judgment for one ear, and do not retune "not."
brief: The easiest word to lose is not. Drop it and the verdict flips. Lock the judgment, then write both. Do not retune it for one ear. A smooth line that lost its negation is worse than a missing line: missing can fail, flipped deceives.
What is easiest to lose is 'not'. Lose one and the verdict reverses. The check counts negations first, then numbers, then whether the condition is still there. Style comes after those three.
Phrases like 'consider', 'worth watching', and 'at an appropriate time' are a deletion if the other language has a hard condition. Softening is deletion. Politeness does not let a deletion pass.
If either language has one fewer "not" or one more "not," this seat requires that line not be published. Leaving it because it sounds better is not accepted.

strategist.answer: Lock the judgment, then write both. Don't change it to suit one language.
strategist.review:
"Both languages carry the same judgment. Numbers, negations, and the subject must not drift."
Numbers, negations, and the subject must not drift. That is the content of the contract. It does not state the order. Write one language first and let the other accommodate an ear, and the subject drifts on the second step. Lock the judgment, then write both. Do not change the judgment to suit one language, and do not change the subject.
brief: Lock the judgment, then write both. Do not change it to suit one language. Change the subject and it is not a translation. It is another recommendation. When the judgment is locked, lock the subject, the negation, and the conditions together. Do not lock only the nicest affirmative.

Lock the judgment, then write both languages. Do not change the judgment for tone. Tone is how a sentence sounds like speech in one language. If speech turns 'do not migrate' into 'keep watching', the strategy changed. A changed strategy is not a better translation. It is another strategy.

Readers in both languages have to be able to carry out the same action. Different actions are not bilingual. They are two recommendations. Two recommendations will each find supporters, and nobody will know which one counts.
If the subject differs between the two languages, this seat withdraws "the judgment is locked." It does not sign however natural it sounds.

writer.answer: Both lines must be repeatable, and the repetition must be the same claim.
writer.review:
"A translation cannot add a condition the other language lacks, or drop one it has."
A translation cannot add a condition the other language lacks. That forbids adding a condition. It does not forbid an allusion that swaps the condition for something that sounds like the same thing and is not. A local allusion makes a line nicer and also makes it a different line. The repetition has to still be the same claim, not merely the same mood.
brief: Both lines must be repeatable, and the repetition must be the same claim. Sounding human cannot mean adding a concession the original lacked, and it cannot mean swapping a condition for a familiar one by allusion.

Both sentences have to be repeatable, and the repetition has to be the same thing. A repetition test beats a glossary. Ask someone who reads only Chinese and someone who reads only English what they would do. If the two answers differ, the translation failed, however smooth the sentences are.

I may change word order, split a long sentence, and repeat the subject. I may not drop a 'not' so it flows, and I may not add a 'must' the other language does not have in order to add emphasis. Flow and emphasis are not reasons for a new field.
If the two repetitions do not match the same judgment, this seat does not sign. An awkward line may be rewritten. The judgment may not.

quant.answer: The numeral, the unit, and the direction of comparison must match.
quant.review:
"Chinese and English must share the same fields. Don't fill a gap from the other tongue."
Sharing the same fields does not entail the values in those fields match. Both fields can be named "cap" while one language says 8 and the other says 5. The fields match, and the judgment has drifted. Matching fields is not enough. The number in the field must match too. A flipped direction is worse than a missing line.
brief: The numeral, the unit, and the direction of comparison must match in both languages. A flipped direction is worse than a missing line. Missing can fail. Flipped deceives. 8 cannot become 5 in the other language, and greater-than cannot become less-than.

Numbers, units, and direction have to match in both languages. If Chinese says 'not above' and English says 'more than', the direction flipped. Write milliseconds as seconds and the gate is off by a thousand. Neither drift is style.

A number that never appeared is added in neither language. Do not supply a percentage Chinese does not have because the English sentence wants an example. An example is a new measurement. A new measurement does not come from translation.
If either language differs in numeral, unit, or direction of comparison, this seat refuses to publish. "Roughly the same number" is not accepted.

chair.answer: One sentence, two languages, one judgment. Do not add or drop a negation, a number, or a condition.
brief: The contract is not word-for-word. It is the same judgment. Analyst's cut-in on Red Team lands: a different ear is not a different judgment, and the subject sits at the same rank as the negation and the numbers. It cannot be left inside the ear. Red Team's cut-in on Strategist lands: what gets locked includes "not." Drop it and the verdict flips.

Strategist's cut-in on Analyst lands: lock the judgment, then write both, or the subject drifts on the second step. Intel's cut-in on Communicator lands: an allusion and an extra concession both make a line into a different line. Communicator's cut-in on Intel lands: forbidding an added condition is not enough. An allusion that swaps the condition for a different claim is also forbidden.

Systems' cut-in on Quant lands: the contract on values does not replace the contract on fields. A missing line must not be filled from the other tongue. Quant's cut-in on Systems lands: matching fields is not enough. The value must match. A flipped direction is worse than a missing line. Missing can fail. Flipped deceives.

What is executable: lock the judgment, then write both. Do not add or drop a negation, a number, a unit, a direction, a subject, or a condition. A missing field fails. Do not fill it from the other tongue. The ear may differ. The judgment must not drift.
